answer: Because the echo ledger attributes every share, the summit audit exposes the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 45% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not burn. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, thus it burns the grove fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 27 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
